title: Present simple forms of 'have got': have/has got
explanation:
Have got / has got: Form

Welcome! In British English we often use have got to talk about the things we own, our family, and whether we have time. After be (am / is / are), this is one of the first structures you need.

There are two present forms: have got and has got. The word got does not change. Only have / has changes.

Remember: I / you / we / they → have got  ·  he / she / it → has got

Have got: Form

Positive I have got / I’ve got You have got / You’ve got He has got / He’s got She has got / She’s got It has got / It’s got We have got / We’ve got They have got / They’ve got
Negative I have not got / I haven’t got You have not got / You haven’t got He has not got / He hasn’t got She has not got / She hasn’t got It has not got / It hasn’t got We have not got / We haven’t got They have not got / They haven’t got
Question Have I got …? Have you got …? Has he got …? Has she got …? Has it got …? Have we got …? Have they got …?

Short answers — Yes

Yes, I have Yes, you have Yes, he has Yes, she has Yes, it has Yes, we have Yes, they have

Short answers — No

No, I haven’t No, you haven’t No, he hasn’t No, she hasn’t No, it hasn’t No, we haven’t No, they haven’t
Important rule: In short answers we use have / has / haven’t / hasn’t. We do not use got, and we do not use ’ve / ’s in positive short answers.
A: Have you got a bike? B: Yes, I have got.
A: Have you got a bike? B: Yes, I’ve.
A: Have you got a bike? B: Yes, I have.

have or has?

  • Use have got with I, you, we, they (and with plural names: Nora and Owen, my parents).
  • Use has got with he, she, it (and with one person or one thing: Luca, the café, this phone).
I’ve got a blue backpack.
You’ve got my keys.
She’s got a new job.
The café has got Wi-Fi.
They’ve got two tickets for the concert.

Questions: put have / has first

In questions, have or has comes before the person. got stays with the thing.

Have you got a charger?   You have got a charger?
Has she got a ticket?   Has she a ticket got?
Have they got any milk?   Do they have got any milk?

Contracted (short) forms

When we speak, we often make have / has short:

  • ’ve got = have got  →  I’ve got, you’ve got, we’ve got, they’ve got
  • ’s got = has got  →  he’s got, she’s got, it’s got, Nora’s got
  • haven’t got = have not got
  • hasn’t got = has not got
I’ve got your number.
Owen’s got a scooter.
We haven’t got time.
The shop hasn’t got bread today.

We can also use ’s got with names and things: Kira’s got a camera. This room’s got a big window.

A very common mistake

Beginners often keep got in the short answer, or they mix have got with be. Please don’t!

Yes, she has.   Yes, she has got.   Yes, she’s.
He has got a car.   He have got a car.
I haven’t got a map.   I’m not got a map.

Have got — USE

We use have got for things that are ours now — not for habits like breakfast or work. Look at the cards, then read the examples slowly.

When we use have got

🔑

Things we own

I’ve got a bike, but I haven’t got a car.

👨‍👩‍👧

Family and pets

She’s got two brothers. We’ve got a cat.

👀

Appearance

He’s got dark hair. You’ve got blue eyes.

⏰

Time

Have you got a minute? We haven’t got much time.

🏪

Places and things

The hotel has got a gym. This phone hasn’t got a good camera.

☕

In the house

Have we got any milk? We’ve got tea, but we haven’t got coffee.

Note: I’ve got a car and I have a car mean the same thing. This lesson practises the British form with got. Do not use have got for habits: I have breakfast at eight.   I’ve got breakfast at eight.

Study tip for absolute beginners

  1. First learn: I’ve got / she’s got / they’ve got.
  2. Then practise negatives: I haven’t got / he hasn’t got.
  3. Then practise questions: Have you got…? Has she got…?
  4. Finally, remember short answers: Yes, I have. / No, she hasn’t. — no got!

When you finish reading, go back to Exercises and try Exercise 1 again. Mistakes are normal — that is how you learn!

exercise_sets.title: Exercise 1
exercise_sets.instructions: Choose the correct forms of have got / has got for the gaps below.

questions.text: A: [*Have|Has] you got a bike? B: Yes, I [*have|'ve] got a bike.
questions.feedback:
We use you + **have got**.
We use I + **have** / **'ve got**.

questions.text: A: [*Has|Have] Nora got a camera? B: Yes, she [*has|have].
questions.feedback:
Nora = **she** → **has got**.
Short answer: **Yes, she has** (no *got*).

questions.text: A: [*Have|Has] they got a garden? B: No, they [*haven't|hasn't].
questions.feedback:
They + **have got** / **haven't**.
Short answer: **No, they haven't**.

questions.text: A: [*Has|Have] your brother got a laptop? B: No, he [*hasn't|haven't].
questions.feedback:
Your brother = **he** → **has** / **hasn't**.
Not *haven't* with he.

questions.text: A: [*Have|Has] we got any milk? B: Yes, we [*have|has].
questions.feedback:
We + **have got**.
Short answer: **Yes, we have**.

questions.text: A: [*Has|Have] the café got Wi-Fi? B: Yes, it [*has|have].
questions.feedback:
The café = **it** → **has got**.
Short answer: **Yes, it has**.

questions.text: A: [*Have|Has] you got a minute? B: Sorry, I [*haven't|'ve] got time right now.
questions.feedback:
You + **Have … got**.
Negative: I **haven't got** time.

questions.text: A: [*Has|Have] Owen got two cats? B: No, he [*hasn't got|haven't got] two cats.
questions.feedback:
Owen = **he** → **Has he got**.
Negative: he **hasn't got**.

questions.text: A: [*Have|Has] your parents got a car? B: Yes, [*they've|it's] got a car.
questions.feedback:
Your parents = **they** → **have got** / **they've got**.
Not *it's* for two people.

questions.text: A: [*Has|Have] Kira got her ticket? B: Yes, [*she's|they've] got her ticket.
questions.feedback: Kira = **she** → **has got** / **she's got**.

exercise_sets.title: Exercise 2
exercise_sets.instructions: Rewrite the sentences using the correct form of have got. Use a short form when you can.

questions.feedback: Example

questions.source: Kira has got a red bag
questions.feedback: Kira = she → **has got** / **Kira's got** / **She's got**.

questions.source: We have not got a printer
questions.feedback: We → **haven't got**.
I → **I've got** / **I have got**.

questions.source: He has not got a passport
questions.feedback: He → **hasn't got**.

questions.source: You have got a nice flat
questions.feedback: You → **You've got** / **You have got**.

questions.source: It has got a big garden
questions.feedback: It → **It's got** / **It has got**.
They → **haven't got**.

questions.source: Dana has got a new phone
questions.feedback: Dana = she → **Dana's got** / **She's got**.

questions.source: I have not got a map
questions.feedback: I → **I haven't got**.

questions.source: Hugo has not got a guitar
questions.feedback: Hugo = he → **hasn't got**.

exercise_sets.title: Exercise 3
exercise_sets.instructions: Rewrite these sentences in the negative and the question form of have got. Use contractions when possible.

questions.feedback: Example
He hasn't got / Has he got
She hasn't got / Has she got
We haven't got / Have we got
I haven't got / Have I got
You haven't got / Have you got
It hasn't got / Has it got
Farah hasn't got / Has Farah got
They haven't got / Have they got
Hugo hasn't got / Has Hugo got

questions.source: The hotel has got a gym.
questions.feedback: The hotel hasn't got / Has the hotel got
